label: Born in Pisa
description: Born from Giulia Ammannati and Vincenzo Galilei.

sources.quote: Galileo was born in Pisa from Giulia Ammannati (1538–1620) and Vincenzo Galilei (1520–1591), a musician, on February 15, 1564

label: Registered at University of Pisa
description: Registered in the faculty of Artists as a student of Medicine.

sources.quote: On November 5, 1581, he was registered in the faculty of Artists at the University of Pisa as a student of Medicine.

label: Met Ostilio Ricci
description: Met the mathematician in Florence and took up Mathematics, leaving Medicine.

sources.quote: In Florence in 1583 he met the mathematician Ostilio Ricci (1540–1603) and took up Mathematics, leaving Medicine, but never graduated.

label: Became Lecturer at University of Pisa
description: Lecturer of Maths with a salary of only 60 ducats/year.

sources.quote: On 1589, he became Lecturer of Maths at the University of Pisa, with a salary of only 60 ducats/year.

label: Experiment of falling spheres
description: Carried out the famous experiment from the Tower of Pisa.

sources.quote: It was in 1590 that he carried out the famous experiment of falling spheres from the Tower of Pisa.

label: Appointed at University of Padua
description: Appointed to take over the vacant chair of Mathematics with a salary of 180 florins/year.

sources.quote: On September 25, 1592, at the early age of 28 years ( Figure 1) he was appointed at the University of Padua to take over the vacant chair of Mathematics with a better salary (180 florins/year)

label: Invented the compass
description: Invented the geometric and military compass during his time in Padua.

sources.quote: He invented the compass (Figure 2), he wrote books on mechanics and cosmography for students.

label: Invented a telescope
description: Invented a telescope with a 18–20 fold magnification.

sources.quote: He invented a telescope (Figure 3), with a 18–20 fold magnification

label: Presented telescope to Doge
description: Presented the telescope to the Doge Leonardo Donato and to the Council of Ten.

sources.quote: On August 24, 1609, he had had the opportunity to present the telescope to the Doge Leonardo Donato and to the Council of Ten of the Serenissima Republic of Venice

label: Observed Jupiter's moons
description: Observed four objects moving around Jupiter during the cold shiny nights of 7-13th January 1610.

sources.quote: The latter observation was made during the cold shiny nights of 7-13th January 1610, when he observed four objects moving around Jupiter

label: Published Sidereus Nuncius
description: Wrote and published quickly the 'Sidereus Nuncius', a book of only 55 pages, dedicated to Cosimo II.

sources.quote: He wrote and published quickly the ''Sidereus Nuncius'' (''celestial announcement''), a book of only 55 pages, dedicated to Cosimo II, and full of notes and drawings proving his observations.

label: Resigned from chair in Padua
description: Resigned having accepted from Cosimo II de' Medici the offer of a chair at the University of Pisa.

sources.quote: Nevertheless, on June 10, 1610, he resigned from the chair in Padua, having accepted from Cosimo II de' Medici the offer of a chair at the University of Pisa

label: Left Padua to move to Florence

sources.quote: On June 15, 1610, Galileo left Padua to move to Florence.

label: Nominated Primary Mathematician at Pisa
description: Nominated as 'Primary Mathematician' at the University of Pisa and Philosopher by the Tuscan Grand Duke Cosimo II.

sources.quote: On July 10, 1610 Galileo was nominated as ''Primary Mathematician'' at the University of Pisa and Philosopher by the Tuscan Grand Duke Cosimo II

label: Visited Rome
description: Visited Rome to meet Pope Paul V and the Roman College of Jesuits.

sources.quote: On April 1611, he visited Rome to meet Pope Paul V and the Roman College of Jesuits, the chief of which, Christopher Clavius (1538–1612) ( Figure 6) fascinated by the observation of Jupiter's moons, reserved him a friendly welcome.

label: Enrolled as member of Lincei Academy

sources.quote: On April 26, 1611 he was enrolled as a member of the Lincei Academy, founded in 1603 by the young Federico Cesi (1585–1630) ( Figure 7)

label: Caccini blamed Galileo
description: Dominican friar Tommaso Caccini violently blamed Galileo from the pulpit of Santa Maria Novella.

sources.quote: The Dominican friar Tommaso Caccini (1574–1648), on December 21, 1614, violently blamed Galileo from the pulpit of Santa Maria Novella in Florence, strongly defending the literal scriptures, and clearly accusing Galileo of heresy.
On February 25, 1616, the Holy Office (Inquisition) officially condemned the Copernican Theory.

label: Bellarmino warned Galileo
description: Cardinal Bellarmino met Galileo and gave him a friendly warning not to sustain, teach, or refer to Copernican theory.

sources.quote: Cardinal Bellarmino met Galileo and gave him a friendly warning not to sustain, teach, or refer to Copernican theory, otherwise the risk was to undergo Inquisition.

label: De revolutionibus prohibited
description: The book by Nicolaus Copernico was prohibited and heliocentric theory was refused.

sources.quote: On March 5, 1616, the book ''De revolutionibus orbium coelestium'' by Nicolaus Copernico was prohibited and heliocentric theory was refused
On August 6, 1623, Cardinal Maffeo Barberini (1568–1644) ( Figure 9), adrmirer of Galileo, was elected Pope with the name of Urban VIII.

label: Published Dialogue
description: The book received the 'nihil obstat' authorisation by the Church Office in Florence, and was published in 1632.

sources.quote: The book received the ''nihil obstat'' authorisation by the Church Office in Florence, and was published in 1632.

label: Brought to trial
description: Brought to trial in the Church of Santa Maria Minerva and charged with heresy.

sources.quote: He was put into jail and in June 1633, brought to trial in the Church of Santa Maria Minerva (Figure 11).

label: Condemned to home arrest
description: Condemned to deny his mistakes and to home arrest for the rest of his life.

sources.quote: He was forced not to treat orally or to write any more on the issue, and condemned to home arrest for the rest of his life.

label: Virginia died
description: His daughter Virginia died prematurely in 1634.

sources.quote: Galileo was confined to his house in Arcetri, not so far from the cloister where his daughter Virginia (1600–1634) (Sister Maria Celeste) was living and where she died prematurely in 1634.
In 1637 Galileo became blind bilaterally (Figure 13), most probably as a final complication of a long-standing reactive arthritis

label: Published Discourses
description: Published with Elzevier a new version of Dialogue, with a different title 'Discourses and Mathematical Demonstrations Relating Two New Sciences'.

sources.quote: In 1638 he published with Elzevier a new version of Dialogue, with a different title ''Discourses and Mathematical Demonstrations Relating Two New Sciences'', confirming his views.

label: Died at Arcetri
description: Died on the same day of his Jupiter observations by telescope.

sources.quote: On January 8, 1642, on the same day of his Jupiter observations by telescope, he died at Arcetri and was buried in a hidden Chapel of Santa Croce Church in Florence

label: Buried in Santa Croce Church
description: Buried in a hidden Chapel of Santa Croce Church in Florence, without any official ceremony.

sources.quote: On January 8, 1642, on the same day of his Jupiter observations by telescope, he died at Arcetri and was buried in a hidden Chapel of Santa Croce Church in Florence

label: Mausoleum built
description: A mausoleum was built in the same church of Santa Croce and his remains were transferred.

sources.quote: In 1737 , a mausoleum was built in the same church of Santa Croce and his remains were transferred together with those of his daughter Virginia.
